lexique.title: Glossary
lexique.meta: CTL, VDOT, thresholds, efficiency — every number of the app, translated.
lexique.missingBody: Definitions grow with each release. Come back through the “?” on any page or the More hub.

ctl.def: Fitness. Your 42-day average load — your “base”: it rises slowly and fades slowly.

atl.def: Fatigue. Your 7-day average load — what you have absorbed recently.

tsb.def: Freshness = fitness − fatigue. Negative during loading phases, positive when you are tapered. The peak-shape number.

acwr.def: Acute load (7 d) / chronic load (28 d) ratio. Above 1.5, the ramp-up is steep: injury risk.

trimp.def: A session's training load, computed from its duration and your heart rate (or a distance equivalent).

vdot.def: Your fitness level as one number (≈ effective VO2max), derived from your best performance. It calibrates every pace in the app.

vma.def: Maximal aerobic speed — the pace at which you consume your maximum oxygen, sustainable for ~6 minutes.

cs.def: The pace you can hold for a long time (~45-60 min). Computed from your 2- to 20-minute efforts.

dprime.def: Anaerobic reserve: the distance you can run above your critical speed before blowing up. A small D′ = diesel profile.

lt1.def: Aerobic threshold: the boundary between easy endurance and sustained work. Below it, you can talk.

lt2.def: Anaerobic threshold: the fastest pace you can hold without accumulating lactate. Close to your critical speed.

ef.def: Metres per minute per heartbeat. It rises when the same heart produces more speed: the marker of your aerobic base.

decoupling.def: Efficiency loss between the first and second half of a run. Under 5%, your endurance holds the distance.

polarization.def: Your volume distribution: ~80% easy, ~20% hard. Avoid the “grey zone” in between.

fatigueExponent.def: How your pace degrades when distance doubles (reference: +4.2%). Measured on your own performances.

negativeSplit.def: Finishing faster than you started — the most reliable racing strategy over long distances.

oneRm.def: One-rep max: the load you can lift a single time, estimated from your strength sets.

rpe.def: Perceived effort, rated from 1 to 10. Complements the numbers when the watch is not enough.

acwr-danger.title: Load rising too fast
acwr-danger.detail: Your recent volume clearly exceeds what your body is used to absorbing. This is the classic configuration that precedes an injury. Plan a lighter week of 30 to 40%.

acwr-caution.title: Load rising markedly
acwr-caution.detail: Nothing alarming, but you are above the comfort zone. Stabilise the volume for one week before ramping up again.

acwr-low.title: Room to increase
acwr-low.detail: Your recent load is below your habit. You can raise volume progressively, without exceeding +10% per week.

volume-jump.title: Weekly volume spike
volume-jump.detail: The +10% per week rule limits the risk of overuse injury. You have gone well past it.

gap.title: Break in training
gap.detail: Aerobic adaptations start fading after about 10 days without stimulus. Resume progressively rather than jumping back to your previous level.
gap.evidence: {days} consecutive days without a run over the last 4 weeks

too-hard.title: Too much intensity, not enough easy
too-hard.detail: The polarised model recommends about 80% of volume in base endurance. Running “moderately hard” too often tires you without building your aerobic base.

no-intensity.title: No fast sessions
no-intensity.detail: Your aerobic base is well trained, but without threshold or VO2max sessions, speed progresses little. One intense session per week is enough.

stale-reference.title: Old performance reference
stale-reference.detail: Your estimated level relies on an effort that is starting to date. A 5 km test or a timed fast run would refine your target paces.

pace-improving.title: Average pace improving
pace-improving.detail: At comparable volume, you run faster than a month ago. That is the sign that the load is well absorbed.

pace-slower.title: Average pace dropping
pace-slower.detail: Not necessarily negative: it happens when volume increases or when you run more endurance. Watch it if it persists with a high HR.

efficiency-up.title: Aerobic efficiency rising
efficiency-up.detail: You run faster for the same heart rate: your aerobic engine is improving.
efficiency-up.evidence: +{pct}% speed per beat vs previous month

efficiency-down.title: Aerobic efficiency falling
efficiency-down.detail: At equal HR you run slower. Accumulated fatigue, heat or lack of recovery are the most common causes.
efficiency-down.evidence: {pct}% speed per beat vs previous month

goal-met.title: Weekly goal held
goal-met.detail: You are at the level you set, on average over the last month.
goal-met.evidence: {avg} km/week for a goal of {goal} km

goal-far.title: Far from the weekly goal
goal-far.detail: Either the goal is too ambitious for now, or one more run per week is needed. An unrealistic goal discourages more than it motivates.
goal-far.evidence: {avg} km/week for a goal of {goal} km

recent-pr.title: New personal record
recent-pr.detail: Your best performances on reference distances date from the last month — you are on an upward curve.

overreaching.title: You are pulling the rope
overreaching.body: Fatigue exceeds your fitness by {gap} points. One or two easy days are enough to get back into building territory.

productive.title: You are building
productive.body: Fatigue exceeds your fitness by {gap} points: that is where progress happens, as long as recovery follows.

neutral.title: You are in balance
neutral.body: Load and recovery offset each other: no fatigue piling up, no fitness eroding.

optimal.title: You are tapered
optimal.body: Freshness of +{gap} on a fitness of {ctl}: the ideal window for a race or a test.

fresh.title: You are fresh, maybe too much
fresh.body: Freshness of +{gap}: well rested, but fitness that stops working eventually declines.

headline.dangerTail: This week's load has jumped compared to the month: increased injury risk.
headline.rampTail: Your fitness is rising fast (+{ramp}/week): watch the signals.

ui.loadNote: Acute load (7 days) compared to chronic load (28 days) shows whether your progression is sustainable.

ui.need2Months: At least 2 months of data required.
ui.scatterHint: bottom left = faster at lower HR
ui.need3Hr: At least 3 sessions with heart rate required.
ui.noHr: No heart-rate data over the period.
ui.intensityNote: Last 28 days, by time actually spent in each zone — not by the session's average HR.
ui.thinCompare: Fewer than 4 runs in one of the periods: changes are hidden.
ui.calendarNote: A year at a glance, then the week ahead
ui.aerobicNote: The pace you hold at a constant heart rate — the most reliable sign of endurance progress, no race needed.
ui.aerobicLine: At {hr} bpm, you now run at
ui.aerobicBetter: {d} s/km gained at the same cardiac effort: your aerobic base is improving.
ui.aerobicWorse: {d} s/km lost at the same effort: fatigue, heat, a break… keep an eye on it if it lasts.
ui.aerobicNoise: A {d} s/km gap, within the margin of error: your aerobic fitness is stable.
ui.aerobicNoHistory: Not enough history yet to compare with three months ago.
ui.aerobicNeed: At least 4 runs with heart rate over 6 weeks (easy runs on flat ground) are needed to measure your pace at fixed HR.
ui.driftGood: Under 5%: your endurance goes the distance.
ui.driftHigh: Over 5%: your heart pays more and more for the same speed late in the run.
ui.aerobicHow: We keep the flat kilometres of your easy runs (no races, no trail, no first km), relate your speed to your heart rate over a rolling 6 weeks, then read the speed at a fixed HR close to your aerobic threshold. The band around the line is the margin of error: the thinner it is, the surer the measure.
ui.aerobicSoon: The curve builds week after week ({n} point(s) so far) — it will sharpen as easy runs with heart rate accumulate.
ui.briefNote: Recap, week ahead, goal, advice — prepared for you, regenerated whenever you want.

footing.name: Easy run + strides
footing.why: Easy volume and a reminder of good form: strides wake the stride without energy cost.

longue-endurance.name: Long endurance run
longue-endurance.why: The marathon pillar: capillary density, glycogen storage, confidence over time.

longue-progressive.name: Long progressive run
longue-progressive.why: Learning to finish fast on tired legs: half and marathon specificity.

allure-marathon.name: Marathon pace · 2 × 6 km
allure-marathon.why: The body memorises race-day pace with fresh legs: specific running economy.

seuil-2x20.name: Threshold · 2 × 20 min
seuil-2x20.why: The signature session: pushes the lactate threshold, the ceiling of sustainable pace.

seuil-fractionne.name: Split threshold · 6 × 5 min
seuil-fractionne.why: Threshold volume without the monotony of a long block, with short recoveries.

vo2max-1000.name: VO2max · 6 × 1,000 m
vo2max-1000.why: Builds cardiac capacity: the session that raises your VDOT.

vo2max-3min.name: VO2max · 5 × 3 min
vo2max-3min.why: Same capacity as the 1,000 m, with shorter reps to come back in shape.

vitesse-300.name: Speed · 10 × 300 m
vitesse-300.why: Mechanics and running economy: the foot lands faster without costing more.

fartlek-suedois.name: Swedish fartlek
fartlek-suedois.why: Intensity by feel: 60 min of variations working the whole spectrum.

cotes.name: Hills · 8 × 45 s
cotes.why: Strength and posture uphill: the specific power missing on the flat.

mixte-competition.name: Race block · 2000 + 1000
mixte-competition.why: Simulates racing: from threshold towards VO2max, the baton pass of competition.

test-vdot.name: Calibration test · 5 km
test-vdot.why: The best fitness signal: an all-out 5 km recalibrates your VDOT and every pace.

racePlan.targetOff: no target time set — indicative paces

racePlan.segmentNote: The target time is spread proportionally to each segment's cost — the sum falls exactly on the total
racePlan.fuelingDefault: Nothing new on race day: everything below must have been tested in training.

racePlan.eve0: Sleep 8 h — the night of D−2 matters more than the night before
racePlan.eve1: Bib, pins, kit, shoes: all laid out the night before
racePlan.eve2: Charge the watch and the phone
racePlan.eve3: No new meals, no alcohol, regular hydration
racePlan.eve4: Read the pace plan once, then stop thinking about it
racePlan.day0: Wake 3 h before the start: tested breakfast, usual coffee
racePlan.day1: Arrive 60-90 min early: bib, toilets, find your corral
racePlan.day3: Held-back start: the plan protects you from first-third euphoria
racePlan.day4: Fuel from the first third, before you get thirsty
racePlan.day5: Last third: everything that's left, mentally
racePlan.deleteConfirm: Delete the GPX and the plan?
racePlan.pitch: Know your course before racing it.
racePlan.pitchBody: Import the course GPX: the app splits it into climbs, descents and flats, spreads your target time at constant effort, then prepares nutrition, the pace band and race-day scenarios.

racePlan.targetPredicted: time estimated from your fitness (adjust below)
racePlan.segmentsNote: Automatic split into homogeneous-gradient segments — each segment's pace follows constant effort (climbs cost more, descents help).
racePlan.scenariosNote: A = the goal, B = realistic (fitness prediction), C = finish in one piece. Cutoffs show the margin.
racePlan.switchSignal: At km {km}, if you pass after {time}, switch to scenario B: the goal is out of reach without burning out.
racePlan.bandNote: Print this page: the table folds into a wrist band. One mark per kilometre, at the target split.
racePlan.debriefNote: {name} compared to the plan, segment by segment.

racePlan.lesson_fade: The end was costly: the start may have been too ambitious or the fuelling too light.
racePlan.lesson_strongFinish: Finished faster than planned: you had margin, aim higher next time.
racePlan.lesson_climbsCostly: Climbs cost you more than planned: add hills to your training.
racePlan.lesson_descentsSlow: You brake on descents: downhill form will save time.
racePlan.list_week_0: Shake the legs, short and sharp without fatigue
racePlan.list_week_1: Carb-load over the last 2-3 days (long races)
racePlan.list_week_2: Cut volume by 40-60%, keep the intensity

racePlan.list_week_4: Scout the trip, bib, start corral and aid stations

racePlan.list_eve_4: Read the plan once, then let it go

racePlan.list_day_1: Arrive 60-90 min early: bib, toilets, corral
racePlan.list_day_3: Held-back start: the plan guards against first-third euphoria

login.footStrava: With Strava, requested permissions: read your profile and activities, including private ones. The app never writes to your Strava account.

errors.throttled: Too many attempts. Try again a little later.
errors.email-taken: An account already exists with this email.
errors.not-allowed: This instance is private: sign-ups are closed.
errors.origin: Request refused. Reload the page and try again.

login.deleted: Your account and all your data have been permanently deleted from this instance.

logPage.title: Log
logPage.howFeelNote: Log through the day — each pass merges with the previous one.
logPage.firstDay: Fill your first day to start the trend.

recap.title: Retrospective
recap.nothingBody: Sync your Strava runs: the retrospective builds itself.

calculator.title: Calculator
calculator.empty: Enter a performance to estimate your level and paces
calculator.backyardNote: A 6.706 km loop every hour, last one standing. Tune the walk share to stay under the hour.

zones.empty: Not enough data for this period yet.

verdict.balanced: Well polarised: mostly easy, with intensity concentrated in a few sessions.
verdict.tooMuchMid: Too much “grey zone”: easy runs are too fast or hard sessions not hard enough. Slow down on easy days.
verdict.tooHard: Under 70% easy: the hard load is high, and recovery often suffers.
verdict.allEasy: Almost all easy: ideal in a base phase — add a quality session when you want to progress.
verdict.thin: Sample too thin to judge (under 4 runs or 3 h): read it as a hint.

zones.noHrData: No heart-rate data for this period.
zones.noPaceData: Threshold pace unknown: log a race or a VMA.

hr.personal: Personal HR zones (threshold measured at {lthr} bpm)

zones.coverage: {sessions} runs: {stream} read second by second, {splits} per kilometre, {average} from the average, {noHr} without HR (counted by pace).
zones.maxHrEstimated: Max HR estimated from your sessions: set it in settings for more accurate zones.
zones.discordHeart: Your heart says harder than your pace (+{n} intensity points): heat, fatigue, hills… or a heart-rate threshold to revisit.
zones.discordPace: Your pace says harder than your heart (+{n} points): a good day, downhills, or a heart-rate sensor dropping out.

custom.title: My workouts
custom.note: Your own workouts, written as in a notebook. Targets stay relative (@threshold, @VMA): they follow your fitness.
custom.name: Name
custom.syntaxRepeats: Repeats: 6×400 @VMA r=1'30 (recovery between reps) · 3×(…) R=3' (recovery between sets)
custom.syntaxSeparators: Separate blocks with + , ; or a new line
custom.previewEmpty: Type your workout: the profile appears as you go.
custom.pacesEstimated: Paces estimated from your easy runs: add a record for more accurate paces.
custom.emptyList: No custom workout yet — create the first one below.
custom.scheduledReplaced: Added to the plan, replacing that day's session ✓
custom.scheduleError: Could not add it to the plan.
custom.watchTitle: Download for your watch: copy to GARMIN/NewFiles, or import into Garmin Connect

import.title: Import
import.metaSome: {n} runs come from files; {pct}% of your history has a detailed heart-rate curve.
import.metaNone: No imported run yet; {pct}% of your history has a detailed heart-rate curve — watch files fill it in.
import.dropNote: FIT, GPX, TCX, or your full account export as a .zip. A run already synced from Strava is completed (curve, km splits, track), never duplicated or overwritten.
import.dropHint: or click to choose — .fit, .gpx, .tcx, .zip (250 MB max per upload)
import.tooLarge: Upload too large (250 MB max): split the export.

err.quota: 20,000-activity limit reached — the rest were skipped

import.howNote: No API or partnership needed: every watch can export its runs.

garmin.title: Garmin — full history
garmin.body: Garmin Connect (web) → account → Privacy settings → Manage your data → Export your data. You get a link to a .zip: drop it as is. Sleep, resting HR and HRV also fill in your log.

garminOne.title: Garmin — one run
garminOne.body: On an activity page in Garmin Connect: ⚙ → Export Original (.fit file, the most complete) or Export to GPX/TCX.

coros.title: Coros
coros.body: Coros app → activity → ⋯ → Export data → .fit. Or from Training Hub: Activities → export.

suunto.title: Suunto
suunto.body: Suunto app → activity → ⋯ → Export → .fit (or .gpx for the track only).

polar.title: Polar
polar.body: Polar Flow (web) → Diary → session → Export session → TCX or GPX. The full account export is accepted too.

apple.title: Apple Watch, Strava, others
apple.body: Any app that exports GPX or TCX works. From Strava: activity → ⋯ → Export GPX (already synced here anyway).

import.privacy: Files are read on this server and then discarded: only the run's numbers, curve and track are kept, in your account only.
import.rate: Many imports in one hour: try again a little later.

nutrition.title: Race nutrition
nutrition.note: Sports-nutrition reference values, timed to your race: carbs, water and sodium per hour, intakes moved off steep climbs and snapped to aid stations.
nutrition.shortRace: Short race: no required intake, just water.
nutrition.carry: To carry between aid stations: at most {n} × {product}.
nutrition.loading: Loading: ~{g} g of carbs per day, over the last {days} days.
nutrition.breakfast: Breakfast: ~{g} g of carbs, {h} h before the start.
nutrition.caffeineNote: Caffeine: ~{mg} mg total, in the second half.
nutrition.measureSweat: Sweat rate unknown: measure it to refine hydration.
nutrition.overDrinking: Careful: the planned drink exceeds your estimated losses — hyponatraemia risk.
nutrition.disclaimer: General reference values, not medical or dietetic advice. Nothing new on race day: everything must have been tested in training.
nutrition.totals: Total: {carbs} g carbs · {fluid} L fluid · {sodium} mg sodium.
nutrition.noStops: No intake needed for this duration.
nutrition.sweatHow: Weigh yourself before and after an hour-long run, without drinking: weight loss ≈ litres lost.

routes.title: Route workshop
routes.metaSome: {km} km of already-run streets, {roads} segments — your territory.
routes.metaNone: No track yet: sync Strava or import files to draw your network.
routes.territoryNote: Each clay stroke is a street you've run; the bolder, the more often you use it. The grey background (OpenStreetMap) shows surrounding streets, to explore further. Click to drop points of interest.
routes.emptyGraph: No network yet: you need runs with GPS tracks (Strava or import).
routes.buildNote: A distance, a habit ↔ discovery slider, and the network proposes three loops. The default start is your most frequent starting point.
routes.noLoop: No loop of this distance found: try another length.
routes.straightsNote: Nearly straight portions of the network, spotted automatically — for your 400 m reps and strides.
routes.savedNote: They auto-match your runs (times run, record).
routes.noRoutes: No saved route — compose a loop or draw below.
routes.clickMap: Click the map to drop the point

why.rest: No effort: this is where adaptation happens.
why.recovery: Very slow, to flush fatigue without adding any.
why.easy: Builds your aerobic base, the foundation of everything else.
why.long: Extends time on feet: endurance and confidence.
why.tempo: Raises the pace you can hold for long without tipping over.
why.threshold: Pushes back the moment your legs burn.
why.intervals: Grows your engine: more oxygen at high intensity.
why.hills: Strength and running economy, without extra impact.
why.fartlek: Learn to vary pace by feel, like in a race.
why.strides: Form and relaxation at speed, without fatigue.
why.race: The goal itself: apply what you've built.
why.strength: Stronger muscles and tendons, a more durable runner.
why.cross: Stimulates the cardio differently, spares the legs.
why.mobility: Flexibility and range, to absorb the load.

skip.quality: Skip only if necessary: this is what makes you progress.
skip.easy: Low cost, the easiest one to keep.

place.taper: Taper: cut volume, keep the edge.

advice.pain: Something hurts: recovery first, don't push through it.
advice.overreach: Acute load is high ({acwr}): ease off next week rather than add.
advice.tired: Low freshness ({tsb}): favour sleep and easy runs.
advice.raceWeek: {days} days before your {km} km race: nothing more to gain, arrive fresh.
advice.racePlan: {days} days before your {km} km race and no race plan: pacing, fuelling, pace band.
advice.taper: Taper week: volume down, intensity kept, lots of sleep.
advice.feeling: {n} runs without a logged feeling: that's what lets the plan adapt.
advice.log: Fill in your log (sleep, fatigue, pain): your advice will be sharper.
advice.fresh: Form is here ({tsb}): the perfect time for a strong session.
advice.base: A steady week: consistency first, intensity will come at the right time.

season.conflict: Two A races are too close for two full blocks: the second stays in maintenance.

brief.note: A coach's note, regenerated on demand: what matters this week, the trend, and the takeaway. The agent only receives aggregates, never your tracks or notes.

backyard.tooSlow: Loop over the hour: too slow — walk less or run faster.
backyard.sleep: {h} h of borrowed sleep beyond 24 h.
backyard.weekly: Training: peak ~{peak} h/week on feet, base ~{base} h, long run ~{long} h.

edition.raceDayBody: {km} km, today. Nothing new: apply the plan, trust the training.
edition.raceEveBody: {km} km in a few days. Nothing more to gain: arrive fresh, the plan protects.
edition.raceAfterBody: The race is behind you: recover, log your feelings, then learn from it.

manchette.raceDay: {name}: race day. Everything you've built, today.
manchette.raceEve: {name} in {days} day(s): rest, sleep, and read the plan once.
manchette.taper: Taper week: the work is done.
manchette.offseason: No race ahead: time to explore.
